cohort: The study included 230 postpartum women under 45 years of age who had undergone a Cesarean section in two private hospitals in Lyari Town, Karachi, Pakistan.
finding: The study found a 33% C-section rate in Lyari Town Karachi, Pakistan, with planned C-sections being more common (63%) than emergency C-sections (37.4%), primarily due to scarred uterus and patient preference, while fetal distress was a key reason for emergency C-sections.
mod_finding: Planned Cesarean Section (CS) (63%) was more prevalent than Emergency CS (37.4%), with scarred uterus and patient preferences being primary reasons for planned CS, and fetal distress being a main reason for emergency CS.
